diagrams.title: Energy bands: conductor, semiconductor, insulator
diagrams.cap: The forbidden gap E<sub>g</sub> decides conduction. Smaller gap → more free carriers at room temperature, so Ge conducts more than Si. Temperature rise lowers a semiconductor's resistance (negative α).

diagrams.title: Magnetic materials classification
diagrams.cap: Transformer and machine cores use soft ferromagnetic materials (silicon steel) because the narrow B–H loop gives low hysteresis loss.

notes: Where: P = polarisation (C/m²), ε<sub>r</sub> = relative permittivity, E = field (V/m); δ = loss angle
Tip: Breakdown: intrinsic, thermal, electrochemical, discharge. Insulators need high dielectric strength and low tan δ; capacitors need high εᵣ.

notes: Where: x/m = amount adsorbed per gram, p = pressure
Tip: Physisorption: van der Waals, multilayer, reversible, falls with T. Chemisorption: chemical bond, monolayer, specific. Uses: gas masks, catalysis, chromatography.

formulas.name: Chemical kinetics
f: 1st order : k = (2.303t) log [aa − x], t2 = 0.693k
notes: Where: k = rate constant, a = initial concentration, x = amount reacted in time t; E<sub>a</sub> = activation energy, R = gas constant, T in K

mistakes.m: Adding an impurity lowers a metal's resistivity
mistakes.c: Impurities add scattering: ρ = ρ<sub>thermal</sub> + ρ<sub>impurity</sub> rises (Matthiessen's rule).

mistakes.m: A metal's resistance falls as it gets hotter
mistakes.c: Metals: resistance rises with temperature; semiconductors and electrolytes: it falls.

mistakes.m: Hard water is caused by sodium salts
mistakes.c: Hardness comes from calcium and magnesium salts.
